CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.

Article 4

1. The objectives of protection for women victims of violence are directed to: a. creating conditions that support the development of the potential of women victims of violence;
b. strengthening the potential already possessed by women victims of violence; and
c. improving the work skills of women victims of violence.
2. The objectives of protection for child victims of violence are directed to: a. providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence; b. reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment; and
c. increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 17

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent violence against women and children, in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the protection of women and children victims of violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children; and
c. disseminating laws and regulations related to the empowerment of women and protection of child victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims of violence.

Article 7

Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 6 is implemented among others by:
a. forming a network in efforts to prevent violence against women;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns with communities, private sector and non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women.

Article 10

1. Empowerment of women victims of violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is implemented through efforts including:
a. job training; and
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. The provision of empowerment for women victims of violence is implemented with the principles of:
a. equality of rights;
b. responsibility;
c. utility and effectiveness; and
d. respect and enforcement of human rights.
3. Implementation of empowerment for women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by related Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.

Prevention of Violence against Women

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 29

1. Guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted regularly every 3 (three) months.

Article 12

1. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in Article 11 letter a is implemented among others by:
a. forming a network in efforts to prevent violence against children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns with communities, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of child victims of violence.
2. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus having the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 5

The stages of protection for women victims of violence include:
a. prevention of violence against women;
b. protection services for women victims of violence; and
c. empowerment of women victims of violence.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect and recognition of rights; danb. equal human dignity.

Article 28

1. The Regional Apparatus that has the duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is obligated to conduct monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of the results of activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence on a regular basis.
2. The reporting of activity results as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted to the Regent through the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and responsibilities in the field of regional development planning.
3. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) involves the forum for handling victims of violence against women and children in a tiered manner.

Article 3

Point a What is meant by "gender responsive" is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and can provide protection to women and children victims of violence.

Point b What is meant by "non-discrimination" is that the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is provided to every woman and/or every child and is not differentiated based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status, and physical or mental condition.

Point h Sufficiently clear.

Point k Sufficiently clear.

Point m Sufficiently clear.

Article 26

1. In addition to P2TP2A as referred to in Article 20, the community may establish forums/groups at the sub-district and village levels that function as P2TP2A networks in the context of implementing efforts to protect women and children victims of violence.
2. The establishment of forums/groups in villages as referred to in paragraph (1) may be facilitated by the Village Government.

Section Three

FPKK

Article 23

1. In order to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence, FPKK is established.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. Regional FPKK;
b. Sub-district FPKK; and
c. Village FPKK.
3. The establishment of Regional FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be determined by the Regent.
4. The establishment of Sub-district FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall be determined by the sub-district head.
5. The establishment of Village FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be determined by the village head.
6. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure and elements of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

2. The objectives of protection for child victims of violence are directed to: a. providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence; b. reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment; and
c. increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

a. equality of rights;

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of child victims of violence.
2. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus having the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SLEMAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 4

b. strengthening the potential already possessed by women victims of violence; and
c. improving the work skills of women victims of violence.
2. The objectives of protection for child victims of violence are directed to: a. providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence; b. reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment; and
c. increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.

5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.

Article 12

1. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in Article 11 letter a is implemented among others by:

c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of child victims of violence.
2. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus having the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 5

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SLEMAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Prevention of Violence against Children

CHAPTER V

Article 17

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent violence against women and children, in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the protection of women and children victims of violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children; and
c. disseminating laws and regulations related to the empowerment of women and protection of child victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims of violence.

Article 28

3. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) involves the forum for handling victims of violence against women and children in a tiered manner.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing of the impending, ongoing and/or occurrence of violence against victims.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
